title: Edict of the Mexican Inquisition Prohibiting the Use of Peyote (1620)
author: Tribunal del Santo Oficio de la Inquisición de México

creators.name: Tribunal del Santo Oficio de la Inquisición de México

summary: An edict of the Mexican tribunal of the Holy Office, issued in Mexico City on 19 June 1620 over the signature of Licenciado Pedro Nabarre de Isla, prohibiting the use of peyote to discover thefts and divine hidden or future events. The inquisitors deny the plant any natural power to produce visions, attribute them to the devil, threaten users with excommunication and proceedings as suspects in the faith, and pardon use before the edict's publication. The Spanish text is hosted as printed by Irving A. Leonard (1896–1996) in American Anthropologist in 1942, with a new English translation.
excerpt: "Mandamos, que deaque adelante ninguna persona de qualquier grado, y condicion que sea pueda vsar ni vse de la dicha yerba, del Peyote ni de otras para los dichos effectos..." ("We order that from now on no person of any rank or condition whatever may use or shall use the said herb, peyote, or any other for the said purposes...")
citation: Tribunal del Santo Oficio de la Inquisición de México, edict against peyote, Mexico City, 19 June 1620, Archivo General de la Nación, Ramo de Inquisición, tomo 289; printed in Irving A. Leonard, "Peyote and the Mexican Inquisition, 1620," American Anthropologist, n.s., 44, no. 2 (1942): 324–26.
rights: Public domain. The 1620 edict is a government document centuries out of copyright. Leonard's 1942 printing appeared in American Anthropologist, for which the Online Books Page serials survey reports no issue renewals and no renewed contributions before 1953; a 1942 US publication not renewed is in the US public domain. The English translation is new to the archive.
transcript:
_[Spanish text as printed by Irving A. Leonard in 1942 from the Archivo General de la Nación, Mexico City, Ramo de Inquisición, tomo 289. Leonard's (sic) markers and abbreviation tildes are retained; line-end hyphenation is closed up.]_

### Nos los Inquisidores contra la heretica pravedad, y apostassia

NOS LOS INQVISIDORES CONTRA LA HERETICA PRAVEDAD, Y APOSTASSIA EN LA Ciudad de Mexico estados, y Prouincias de la Nueua España, nueua Galicia, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Yucatan, Verapaz, Honduras, Yslas philipinas, y su distrito, y iurisdicion por authoridad Appostolica. &c. Por quanto el vso de la Yerba o Raiz llamada Peyote, para el effecto que en estas Prouincias se ha introducido de descubrir hurtos, y adebinar otros succesos, y futuros cõtingentes occultos, es accion supersticiosa y reprouada oppuesta à la pureça, y sinceridad de nuestra Santa Fee Catholica, siendo ansi, que la dicha yerba, ni otra alguna no pueden tener la virtud, y eficacia natural que se dize para los dichos effectos ni para causar las ymagines, fantasmas y representaciones en que se fundan las dichas adeuinaciones, y que en ellas se vee notoriamente la sugestion, y asistencia del demonio, autor deste abuso, valiendose primero para introduzirle de la facilidad natural de los Indios, y de su inclinacion à la idolatria, y deribondose _(sic)_ despues à otras muchas personas poco temerosas de Dios, y de fee muy informe, con cuyos excesos ha tomado mas fuerça el dicho vicio, y se comete con la frequencia que se hecha deuer _(sic)_. Y deuiẽdo Nos por la obligacion de nuestro cargo atajarle, y occurrir à los daños, y graues offensas de Dios nuestro Señor, que del resultan. Auiendolo tratado, y conferido con personas doctas, y de rectas conciencias, acordamos dar la presente para vos, y à cada vno de vos, por la qual exortamos, requirimos, y en virtud de santa obediencia y sopena de excomunion mayor latae sententiae trina Canonica monitione praemissa, y de otras penas pecuniarias, y corporeles _(sic)_ à nuestro arbitrio reseruodas _(sic)_. Mandamos, que deaque adelante ninguna persona de qualquier grado, y condicion que sea pueda vsar ni vse de la dicha yerba, del Peyote ni de otras para los dichos effectos, ni para otros semejantes, debajo de ningun titulo, o color, ni hagan que los indios ni otras personas las tomen con apercibimiento que lo contrario haciendo, demas deque abreys incurrido en las dichas Censuras y penas, procederemos contra los q̃ rebeldes e inobediẽtes fueredes, como cõtra personas sospechosas en la santa fee Catholica.

Y por quãto el dicho delicto ha estado hasta aqui tã introducido, y vsado como se sabe, y nuestra intencion es prohibirle, y remediarle para adelante, y aquietar las concienias de las personas que le an cometido queriendo vsar de venignidad, y de la comissiõ que para ello tenemos del Illustrissimo señor confesor de su Magestad, Inquisidor General en todos sus Reynos, y Señorios, concedemos gracia, y remission de todo lo passado en el dicho excesso hasta el dia de la publicacion deste nuestro Edicto, y prohibicion, y cometemos à qualasquiera _(sic)_ confesores seculares o regulares approbados por sus Ordinarios, licencia, y facultad para absoluer del dicho delicto [â?] los que como dicho es le vuieren cometido hasta aqui. Con tal que la dicha absolucion no se estienda à lo venidero ni [â?] otros delictos, excesos hechicerias, y supersticiones de las contenidas en el Edicto general de la fee, y en los demas que en esta raçon hemos mandado publicar los quales han de quedar en su fuerça, y obseruancia, y porque lo contenido en esta carta venga à noticia de todos, y nadie lo pueda ygnorar, mandamos que se publeque _(sic)_ en todas la Ciudades Villas, y lugares de nuestro distrito. Dada en la Sala de nuestra Audiencia à diez y nueue dias del mes de Iunio de mill y seiscientos y veinte años.

Ldo D. Pedro Nabarre de Ysla (Rúbrica)
translationNote: Prepared for the archive from Leonard's printed Spanish text, kept close to the edict's legal phrasing; it has not yet been checked by a second reader. Leonard's own 1942 translation gives the date as 29 June, but his Spanish reads "diez y nueue" (nineteen), which is followed here. Translation drafted with AI assistance in October 2026; not yet reviewed by a human translator.
translationText:
### We, the Inquisitors against heretical depravity and apostasy

We, the Inquisitors against heretical depravity and apostasy in the City of Mexico, the states and provinces of New Spain, New Galicia, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Yucatán, Verapaz, Honduras, the Philippine Islands, and their district and jurisdiction, by apostolic authority, etc. Inasmuch as the use of the herb or root called peyote, which has been introduced in these provinces for the purpose of discovering thefts and divining other events and hidden future contingencies, is a superstitious and condemned act, opposed to the purity and sincerity of our Holy Catholic Faith; it being certain that neither the said herb nor any other can have the natural virtue and efficacy claimed for these purposes, nor for causing the images, phantasms, and representations on which these divinations are founded; and that in them the suggestion and assistance of the devil, author of this abuse, is plainly seen, who availed himself first, in introducing it, of the natural credulity of the Indians and their inclination to idolatry, and afterward spread it to many other persons with little fear of God and an unformed faith, through whose excesses the said vice has gained strength and is committed with the frequency now observed. And since the obligation of our office requires us to cut it short and to remedy the harms and grave offenses to God our Lord that result from it, having discussed and conferred on the matter with learned persons of upright conscience, we have agreed to issue the present letter to you and to each one of you, by which we exhort and require you, in virtue of holy obedience and under penalty of major excommunication _latae sententiae_, the threefold canonical warning having been given, and of other pecuniary and corporal penalties reserved to our discretion. We order that from now on no person of any rank or condition whatever may use or shall use the said herb, peyote, or any other for the said purposes or for others like them, under any title or pretext, nor cause the Indians or other persons to take them; with the warning that if you do the contrary, besides having incurred the said censures and penalties, we will proceed against those of you who are rebellious and disobedient as against persons suspect in the holy Catholic faith.

And inasmuch as the said offense has until now been so widespread and practiced, as is known, and our intention is to prohibit and remedy it from now on and to quiet the consciences of the persons who have committed it, wishing to act with leniency, and by the commission we hold for this purpose from the Most Illustrious Lord Confessor of His Majesty, Inquisitor General in all his kingdoms and dominions, we grant grace and remission of everything past in the said excess up to the day of the publication of this our edict and prohibition; and we commit to any confessors, secular or regular, approved by their ordinaries, license and faculty to absolve from the said offense those who, as stated, have committed it up to now. Provided that the said absolution does not extend to the future, nor to other offenses, excesses, sorceries, and superstitions among those contained in the General Edict of the Faith and in the others we have ordered published on this matter, which are to remain in force and observance. And so that what this letter contains may come to the notice of all and no one may be ignorant of it, we order that it be published in all the cities, towns, and places of our district. Given in the hall of our audience on the nineteenth day of the month of June of the year sixteen hundred and twenty.

Licenciado D. Pedro Nabarre de Ysla (rubric)

draft.rationale: The founding colonial prohibition of peyote, issued by the Mexican Inquisition in 1620; later peyote prosecutions in New Spain and modern legal histories of the plant start from it. It adds the institutional, legal response to the archive's colonial records of peyote and ololiuhqui use.

textSource.scope: The Spanish document appended to Leonard's brief communication, American Anthropologist 44, no. 2 (1942), p. 325 (scan leaf n158). Leonard's introductory remarks (pp. 324–25) and his translation (p. 326) are not reproduced. The raw file is the full OCR of the issue.

textQuality.notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 325, using the Internet Archive OCR only as a starting point. OCR errors corrected against the image: 'Espafia'/'Sefior'/'dafios'/'afios' to España/Señor/daños/años; '4' to à throughout; 'cétingentes', 'deuiédo', 'inobediétes', 'ctra', 'quato', 'ta', 'comissi6' restored to the printed tilde forms cõtingentes, deuiẽdo, inobediẽtes, cõtra, quãto, tã, comissiõ; 'G rebeldes' to q̃ rebeldes; 'fuerga'/'ragon' to fuerça/raçon; 'L* PD.' to Ldo D. (the 'do' is superscript in print); 'Rdbrica' to Rúbrica. The printed 'remis ion' has a damaged or missing letter and is given as remission, as the sense and Leonard's translation ('remission') require. Leonard's (sic) markers are his, not the archive's. Spellings such as concienias, qualasquiera, and publeque are left as printed. This is Leonard's transcription of the AGN manuscript; it has not been checked against the manuscript itself, and Leonard does not say whether the AGN copy is manuscript or a printed broadside.
uncertainReadings: [â?] in 'absoluer del dicho delicto â los que' and 'ni â otros delictos': the accent on these two words looks like a circumflex in the scan, where every other instance is a grave accent (à); it may be a broken sort.
Date: Leonard's Spanish has 'diez y nueue' (19 June), his English translation '29th day of June'; secondary literature cites both.
